name: Roosevelt Avenue-Style Cemita Sandwiches

cookwares.name: two 12-inch cast iron skillets or one large griddle

ingredients.name: thin tomato slices, from 2 medium tomatoes
chipotle chilis, canned in adobo sauce

instructions.primary_message: Halve the cemita buns. Halve, pit, and slice the ripe avocados. Shred the iceberg lettuce.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 cemita buns
2 medium ripe avocados
½ cup iceberg lettuce, from 1 small head

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 350°F. Heat 2 cast-iron skillets or 1 large griddle over medium-high heat until lightly smoking. Rub with oil using a paper towel and toast cut surfaces of buns, pressing down with a sturdy spatula to compress. Set aside.
Spread refried beans on bottom buns. Top with meat of choice. Arrange avocado on top of meat.
Top avocado with lettuce, tomato, onion, and papalo. Tear each chipotle into pieces and arrange on top of papalo. Mound cheese strands on top.

Smear top buns with mayonnaise and close sandwiches. Set on baking sheet and transfer to oven until just warmed through and cheese is just starting to soften throughout, about 3 minutes. Or wrap in foil to warm bun and soften cheese, just like they do at the taco truck. Serve.

description: Cemitas have taken on a life of their own in New York City. Here's how to make one like those served in taco trucks along Roosevelt Avenue in Jackson Heights.
notes:
Optional substitutions: cemita buns → sesame-seed buns or brioche buns; warm pork carnitas → al pastor or carne asada or carne adovada or taco filling; Canola oil → vegetable oil; papalo cilantro leaves → fresh cilantro leaves

Notes: Cemita buns, papalo, and queso Oaxaca can be found at well-stocked Mexican and Latin American bakeries and grocers. Queso Oaxaca should be shredded by hand into very thin strands, just like string cheese. Cilantro can be used in place of the papalo.
author: Daniel Gritzer
